chapter: Arranging career and the JPJ Quartet
title: Tunes for Woody Herman, Georgie Auld and Gene Krupa
summary: Budd wrote 'Concerto for Tenor' for Georgie Auld, an arrangement of Redman's 'Cherry' for Herman, and 'What's This' for Krupa.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Beautiful. Now any more of the guys down there here?
Well, now, you said some of the tunes.

With Woody Herman I wrote a tune for Auld Woody Herman when I was arranger for Georgia Auld All. And Woody Herman at this time was recording the different tenor players with his band, and he had recorded Georgia Auld All and I wrote Auld a tune for Georgia Auld All called Concerto for Tenor, a tenor saxophone. That Georgia recorded with him and then I recorded with Woody Herman and wrote an arrangement on Don Redman's Cherry, and recorded that. Ben Webster also recorded with him at this time, and with Gene Krupa I wrote a tune -- I kind of got rooked out of this a little bit because Dave Lambert came up with the idea, and I had to formulate it and everything, but he got the credit for the tune but it's my arrangement on the tune called What's This. And I think it was a very fine arrangement, that's when Gene had 12 strings in his band and Charlie Ventura was playing in that band, and you know, a lot of the guys.
